To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the task of object-interaction recognition is inherently ambiguous, and (2) modelling the ambiguity of object interaction recognition as probabilistic multi-labeling leads to better classification results than conventional single-label classification.
(i) we show that semantic ambiguity in verbs results in legitimate class overlaps, and (ii) we show that learning from probabilistic annotations improves classification of object interactions.

(a) the use of probabilistic multi-label classification enables better recognition performance for object interaction recognition; (b) the use of annotation probabilities for learning a probabilistic multi-class classifier outperforms majority vote and enables discovery of sub-interactions and co-occurring verbs; (c) our method is robust and generalizable to different datasets.
